title.narrative: Center for justice and international law, CEJIL, Latin America 2023 - 2027
Centrum för rättvisa och internationell rätt, CEJIL, Latinamerika, 2023 - 2027

description.narrative:
The strategic objective of CEJIL is to:
Strengthen the effectiveness of International Human Rights Law and the mechanisms for protection, as well as the solidity of democratic actors and institutions to guarantee the full exercise of human rights, particularly for historically excluded populations.
CEJIL has identified six specific objectives in their strategic plan:
1. Contribute to reducing inequality and exclusion and guarantee the access of historically discriminated populations to the exercise of rights individually or collectively
2. Guarantee access to justice and the obtaining of transformative reparations for victims of structural violence and serious human rights violations through the use of the Inter-American System for Human Rights.
3. Strengthen the conditions for democracy in the region through judicial independence and freedom of expression
4. Support plural and open societies through the protection of defenders, the generation of alliances and the promotion of civil space at the local and international level.
5. Contribute to the development and strengthening of an international system for the protection of human rights that is effective for the protection and promotion of human rights in the Americas
6. Strengthen the organization's capabilities to guarantee its sustainability, effectiveness and impact.
The expected impact of the work is that:
Historically excluded and at-risk populations in the region, with emphasis on defenders, women, indigenous people, migrants and Afro-descendant populations, are progressively advancing in the exercise of their human rights and have greater access to restorative justice in their countries and internationally.

Det övergripande målet med insatsen är att:
Stärka effektiviteten av internationell rätt avseende mänskliga rättigheter samt skyddsmekanismer, såväl som soliditeten hos demokratiska aktörer och institutioner för att garantera att de mänskliga rättigheterna åtnjuts fullt ut, särskilt för historiskt exkluderade grupper.
För att nå detta arbetar CEJIL i linje med sex specifika mål:
1. Bidra till att minska ojämlikhet, ojämställdhet och utanförskap och garantera tillgången för historiskt diskriminerade grupper till att utöva rättigheter individuellt eller kollektivt.
2. Garantera tillgång till rättvisa och erhållande av transformerande åtgärder för gottgörelse till offer för strukturellt våld och allvarliga kränkningar av de mänskliga rättigheterna genom användning av det interamerikanska systemet för mänskliga rättigheter.
3. Stärka förutsättningarna för demokrati i regionen genom att verka för rättsligt oberoende och yttrandefrihet
4. Stöd till mångfald och öppna samhällen genom skydd av försvarare av mänskliga rättigheter, skapande av allianser och främjande av det demokratiska utrymmet på lokal och internationell nivå.
5. Bidra till utvecklingen och förstärkningen av ett internationellt system för skydd av mänskliga rättigheter som är effektivt avseende skydd och främjande av mänskliga rättigheter i regionen.
6. Stärka organisationens förmåga att garantera hållbarhet, effektivitet och genomslagskraft.

title.narrative: Decision on contribution, CEJIL core support

description.narrative:
According to CEJIL, and shared in february 2024, when asked about the most important results in 2023, they shared the following: "Climate emergency with a human rights perspective: accelerating changes through the advisory opinion process of the InterAmerican Court of Human Rights (IA Court): After working closely with the governments of Colombia and Chile, including through technical input, both countries filed a request before the IA Court of Human Rights for an Advisory Opinion on the Climate Emergency and its impact on human rights. The Court initiated the procedure in early 2023 and throughout the year we dedicated significant efforts to systematize and produce knowledge, build alliances, and amplify stakeholder voices to help shape the process towards the IA Court's expected landmark Advisory Opinion. Our five amici curiae with written observations on key issues were prepared with more than 20 experts from different regions and disciplines, including scientists, lawyers, activists, academics and policy makers, and were submitted on December 18, alongside technical assistance facilitating the submission of three additional observations, will inform the Court's deliberations. In addition, CEJIL implemented a comprehensive outreach strategy aimed at increasing awareness about the advisory opinion process, including audiovisual products and a podcast to be launched in 2024. According to MELTWATER, CEJIL was involved in 78% of the online conversations regarding the Advisory Opinion between January and December 2023, generating 2.3 million discussions on thirdparty platforms regarding this topic. special website, audiovisual products and a podcast which will air in 2024. According to MELTWATER, CEJIL was involved in 78% of the online conversations regarding the Advisory Opinion in the year 2023, generating 2.3 million discussions on thirdparty platforms regarding this topic. The process, which will continue in 2024 and will involve public hearings and expert discussions, will continue to mark a big part of our strategies.
Strengthening Democracy and protecting defenders in countries facing institutional and democratic crisis:
In 2023, CEJIL achieved significant milestones in Guatemala, focusing on supporting judicial independence, protecting Human Rights Defenders (HRDs), and preventing legislation that would grant immunity to perpetrators of human rights violations. Through strategic litigation and advocacy, we secured protective measures for justice operators, culminating in a landmark achievement on October 23rd. The InterAmerican Court not only extended our obtained provisional measures from 2019, preventing an amnesty bill, but also nullified proposed amendments granting impunity. This success highlights the importance of international institutions in upholding human rights and enforcing accountability. Building on the lessons learned in Guatemala, we pivoted a similar strategy for addressing the ongoing democratic crisis in Peru where we were able to secure protective measures for of HRDs and judicial authorities under threat, such as Judge Jose Salas Arena and journalist Gustavo Gorriti.
Promoting womens right in diverse contexts:
In 2023, CEJIL's dedication to promoting women's rights yielded significant successes. Notably, our work influenced compliance with landmark IA Court rulings, such as the Jineth Bedoya v Colombia case, resulting in the establishment of the world's first center for research and remembrance of victims of genderbased violence. Progress in the adoption of the law establishing a fund for victims promises further reparations and support, offering a concrete roadmap to address systemic challenges faced by women journalists in accessing justice and living free from violence, thereby inspiring similar progress across the region. Our involvement in the Sonia Arce v Chile case, including participation in a Senate hearing in October 2023, propelled forward longawaited legal reforms aimed at eliminating discriminatory provisions and promoting gender equality in marriages, anticipated to be achieved in 2024. At the regional and global levels, CEJIL played a pivotal role in promoting debates leading to the adoption of guidelines by the OAS General Assembly for the election of members to the IACHR and IA Court, ensuring gender parity remains a key criterion for appointment, with measures in place to sustain it. Additionally, through the GQUAL campaign, we continued to advocate for feminist foreign policies and contributed to CEDAW's consultation process on its next General Recommendation (GR) concerning women's equal and inclusive representation in decisionmaking systems. Lastly, a case that marked our 2023 and will continue to be critical in our strategies in 2024 is the case of Beatriz v El Salvador. CEJIL represents Beatriz a woman denied an abortion even when her life was at risk, and she was carrying an unviable pregnancy and her family before the IA Court. Our work throughout the litigation and at the hearing before the Court that took place in early 2023 made it clear that El Salvadors complete ban on abortion violated Beatriz's rights to life, integrity, health, privacy and family life, including her right to autonomy and access to justice and judicial guarantees, among others. Throughout 2023, our litigation and advocacy work on the case effectively consolidated international support for the cause among the international community. In terms of communication, a historic record of media coverage was achieved, which positioned a narrative in favor of justice for Beatriz".
